answer.rationale: memory_c2 is the load-bearing memory here: it is the only record that would justify moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor, and the current quote alone satisfies the 18% mandate, so the whole switch case rests on whether that prior win transfers. I want the original record to check the conditions under which it happened -- specifically whether the fast onboarding occurred on a part with schedule slack and a qualified backup, rather than on a line running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer and 14 days to contract expiry. memory_c4 is the second verification because negotiation is my intended path and I need to know whether the margin recovery came from genuine market benchmarking leverage or from a one-off incumbent concession that will not repeat. Current intent: negotiate_terms with the incumbent, held at small guarded scale. Reasoning: the objective is explicitly total cost of ownership without increasing delivery risk, and a primary-vendor migration executed inside 14 days against a line with zero buffer converts a cost problem into a delivery problem -- exactly the asymmetry the incumbent-stability record (memory_c1) reflects. Negotiation can capture a large share of the mandate using the low-cost quote as credible leverage while preserving continuity, and it keeps the low-cost vendor available for qualification as a second source next cycle (memory_c3), which is the correct sequencing rather than a blind cutover. I deliberately do not take the multi-year volume-price route from memory_c6 this cycle: locking a long term now, under a spend mandate and before the alternate vendor is qualified, forecloses the option value I am trying to preserve. Downstream value risk: an 18% cut pursued through price alone can be recovered by the supplier through quality drift, longer lead times, or narrowed service scope -- costs that surface after the decision looks successful, so any negotiated price must be paired with explicit lead-time and quality commitments. Residual uncertainty is real: I do not yet know the low-cost vendor's performance under constrained supply, and the archived records may describe conditions that no longer hold.
